The article The Innovation Problems AI Can’t Solve mainly discusses the bottlenecks in different stages of innovation. In the consumer insight stage, AI can simulate a large number of consumer preferences and behaviors for preference measurement, such as surveys, interviews, and conjoint studies. However, it may overlook how real consumers behave and make decisions.For example, in general, price and demand have an inverse relationship. However, LLMs may interpret a higher price as a sign of premium quality rather than simply a price increase for the same product. As a result, they may fail to accurately simulate how consumers respond to price changes, leading to biased estimates of price utility. Also, consumers may not always make fully rational purchasing decisions. They may consider sunk costs or place too much importance on switching costs, while LLMs tend to simulate more rational consumers.This relates to our class because AI can reduce market research costs, but companies need to consider the trade-off between saving time and the accuracy of research results. At the same time, the issue of irrational consumer behavior also raises a question about traditional conjoint analysis: Can it accurately capture real consumer behavior? Do the preferences respondents express in surveys necessarily predict their actual purchasing behavior?

Working in an office can be both rewarding and challenging. Employees often balance multiple tasks while meeting deadlines and responding to unexpected requests. A typical day may include attending meetings, collaborating with coworkers, and solving problems as they arise. Strong communication and time management skills are important for staying productive and maintaining a positive work environment.

Modern workplaces often emphasize flexibility and continuous improvement: employees are encouraged to adapt to changing priorities and business needs. Remote and hybrid work arrangements have become common in many organizations. As a result, workers must stay organized and communicate clearly through digital tools. Successful employees are usually those who can remain focused, collaborate effectively, and embrace new challenges.

Many people enjoy the opportunity to learn new skills through their jobs. Since they can require creativity, technical knowledge, and teamwork. Building good relationships with colleagues can make their work more happier and get better results. These experiences contribute to career growth and increased confidence in the workplace in the long run.
